text: Wartime agents' typical slip in a transposition: one column read at the wrong time (a wrong number in the key's numbering), or two columns swapped. Sanborn says his mistakes are on purpose.

Every such slip around every keyword columnar the record closed (this part: one word, the same word twice, interrupted key; the other three are 0203), each slipped route and its inverse, then or before a repeating key of 1-26 on the sculpture's tables, K4 against ten scrambled copies and a planted slip per family.

In each family the shortest key that fits K4 is no shorter than on the copies, and K4 leads every copy in no more cells than a copy does. Planted slips: F6/1 found, F6.16 found, F6.18 NOT found, F11.2 NOT found.
